reasoning: The core problem — which prompt surface features drive a model's inference it is being evaluated, and whether removing them reduces that inference — is directly addressed by recent work. "Is Evaluation Awareness Just Format Sensitivity?" (arXiv 2603.19426) uses a 2x2 controlled toggle of exactly the proposed features (MCQ vs free-response, lettered vs numbered, eval boilerplate) on open and closed models, the same minimal-pairs design. "Do LLMs Know They Are Being Tested? ...GPT-OSS-20B" (arXiv 2510.08624) does cue-identification plus ablation removing individual cues on an open model and asks it to estimate eval-probability — matching the proposed confirmatory ablation and 0-100 rating. The surface-cue catalogue (MCQ, lettered options, eval boilerplate, sterile phrasing) is already enumerated across the "Often Know When Being Evaluated" paper and Alignment Forum framework posts, and directly asking models to rate eval-probability has been tried (with a known failure: models over-classify everything as an eval). The only unexplored increment is the specific "fit a logistic model to rank cues, then confirmatory ablation of the single top cue" pipeline, which is a minor methodological repackaging of work already published.

evidence.title: Is Evaluation Awareness Just Format Sensitivity? Limitations of Probe-Based Evidence under Controlled Prompt Structure
evidence.summary: Uses a 2x2 controlled design that systematically toggles individual formatting features (multiple-choice vs free-response, lettered vs numbered options, eval boilerplate) on open and closed models to isolate which surface features drive apparent evaluation awareness. Concludes much 'eval awareness' is format sensitivity. This is essentially the proposed minimal-pairs single-feature-toggle method.

evidence.title: Do LLMs Know They Are Being Tested? Evaluation Awareness and Incentive-Sensitive Failures in GPT-OSS-20B
evidence.summary: On an open model (GPT-OSS-20B), identifies surface cues signaling evaluation, runs ablation studies removing individual cues to determine which drive eval detection, and prompts the model to explicitly estimate the probability it is being evaluated. Directly matches the proposed open-model eval-probability rating plus confirmatory cue-removal ablation.

evidence.title: Large Language Models Often Know When They Are Being Evaluated
evidence.summary: Documents that models recognize common surface features as eval signals (multiple-choice format, verifiable-solution tasks, performance-eliciting system prompts, synthetic inputs), establishing the surface-cue catalogue the proposal targets.

evidence.title: Evaluation Awareness Scales Predictably in Open-Weights Large Language Models
evidence.summary: Studies eval awareness across 15 open-weights models (0.27B-70B). Notes that directly asking a model to estimate the probability a prompt is an evaluation performs poorly because models classify most prompts as evaluations regardless — a key failure mode the proposed 0-100 rating approach would rediscover, and that models pattern-match to historically eval-correlated surface features.

evidence.title: Comparative Analysis of Black Box Methods for Detecting Evaluation Awareness in LLMs
evidence.summary: Catalogues the cues that tip models off (eval-specific terminology, grading/submission tools, formal/constrained interaction patterns, multiple-choice formatting) and notes labeled A-D options are a near-perfect classifier of test prompts, covering the cue-ranking goal of the proposal.
